brief: Deutsche Bank recaps the September FOMC: the Fed hiked 25bp to 3-3/4 to 4%, matching DB's long-held call, but the dot plot came in more hawkish than DB expected. Sixteen officials see another 2026 hike; 2027 splits between 50 and 75bp more tightening; the long-run dot rose to 3.2%. Chair Warsh gave no forward guidance, framing the hike as removing a "dose" of accommodation despite limited evidence financial conditions are restrictive, citing stronger growth, firmer labor data, sticky inflation, and geopolitical inflation risk versus July. The statement's inflation paragraph hardened, dropping the supply-shock justification for above-target inflation, which DB reads as officials no longer looking through it. In the SEP, the 2026 median rate hit 4.125% as expected, but 2027-28 medians rose 50bp more than DB anticipated, which DB says backs its own quarterly-hike call. Warsh attributed higher long-term yields to growth strength, AI-linked capex and hyperscaler issuance competing for capital, and geopolitical commodity pressure. DB still forecasts 50bp more tightening, in December and March, unwinding last year's risk-management cuts, with upside risk of an October hike.
